1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * vendor/drivers/drivers/rk806/rk806.c
3:  *
4:  * Rockchip RK806 PMIC regulator driver (lower-half).
5:  *
6:  * RK806 is a multi-channel PMIC used on the kickpi-k7 (RK3576) board:
7:  * several BUCK (DCDC) and LDO outputs, each independently switchable and
8:  * voltage-adjustable (discrete voltage tables).
9:  *
10:  * This file provides the lower-half regulator implementation registered
11:  * onto the NuttX regulator upper-half framework
12:  * (include/nuttx/power/regulator.h). Each BUCK/LDO output gets its own
13:  * struct regulator_desc_s + regulator_ops_s and is registered via
14:  * regulator_register().
15:  ****************************************************************************/
16: 
17: #include <nuttx/compiler.h>
18: #include <nuttx/config.h>
19: 
20: #ifdef CONFIG_REGULATOR_RK806
21: 
22: #include <debug.h>
23: #include <errno.h>
24: #include <string.h>
25: 
26: #include <nuttx/i2c/i2c_master.h>
27: #include <nuttx/kmalloc.h>
28: #include <nuttx/power/regulator.h>
29: 
30: #include "rk806.h"
31: #include "rk806_hw.h"
32: 
33: /****************************************************************************
34:  * Pre-processor Definitions
35:  ****************************************************************************/
36: 
37: /* The RK806_ID_* output IDs and RK806_NUM_OUTPUTS live in rk806.h: the board
38:  * side uses the same IDs to configure each rail before registration.  The
39:  * enum value doubles as the selector-family discriminator used by the voltage
40:  * decode helpers (BUCK vs LDO), and is stored in each regulator_desc_s.id by
41:  * the RK806_*_REG descriptor macros.
42:  */
43: 
44: _Static_assert(RK806_NUM_REGULATORS == RK806_NUM_OUTPUTS,
45:                "RK806 descriptor count does not match the output ID enum");
46: 
47: /****************************************************************************
48:  * Private Types
49:  ****************************************************************************/
50: 
51: /* Chip-side metadata for one RK806 output.  Everything here is fixed by the
52:  * PMIC itself; the board-specific name, limits, parent and flags come from
53:  * the table passed to rk806_initialize().
54:  */
55: 
56: struct rk806_hw_s
57: {
58:   unsigned int vsel_reg;
59:   unsigned int vsel_mask;
60:   unsigned int enable_reg;
61:   unsigned int enable_mask;
62:   unsigned int n_voltages;
63: };
64: 
65: /* The RK806 driver private state.
66:  *
67:  * A single global instance is used: the RK806 is a chip-level device, and
68:  * this driver is expected to be initialized exactly once during board
69:  * bring-up.  The instance holds the I2C lower-half pointer and the resolved
70:  * bus parameters, and is shared by all BUCK/LDO regulator callbacks (which
71:  * receive it back through the regulator framework's `priv` pointer).
72:  */
73: 
74: struct rk806_dev_s
75: {
76:   FAR struct i2c_master_s *i2c; /* I2C lower-half driver instance */
77:   uint16_t addr;                /* I2C slave address */
78:   uint32_t frequency;           /* I2C bus frequency */
79: };
80: 
81: /****************************************************************************
82:  * Private Data
83:  ****************************************************************************/
84: 
85: /* Global, statically-initialized private state for the single RK806 device.
86:  *
87:  * The per-output regulator descriptors and ops are declared as
88:  * file-scope static tables below (g_rk806_regulators[] and g_rk806_ops);
89:  * this instance is shared by all of them through the regulator
90:  * framework's `priv` pointer.
91:  */
92: 
93: static struct rk806_dev_s g_rk806 = {
94:   NULL,              /* i2c */
95:   RK806_I2C_ADDRESS, /* addr */
96:   RK806_BUS_SPEED,   /* frequency */
97: };
98: 
99: /****************************************************************************
100:  * Name: rk806_decode_buck_voltage
101:  *
102:  * Description:
103:  *   Return the microvolt value for a BUCK output selector (piecewise).
104:  *
105:  ****************************************************************************/
106: 
107: static uint32_t rk806_decode_buck_voltage(unsigned int selector)
108: {
109:   if (selector < RK806_BUCK_SEL_END0)
110:     {
111:       return RK806_BUCK_VOLT_MIN0 + selector * RK806_BUCK_VOLT_STEP0;
112:     }
113:   else if (selector < RK806_BUCK_SEL_END1)
114:     {
115:       return RK806_BUCK_VOLT_MIN1 +
116:              (selector - RK806_BUCK_SEL_END0) * RK806_BUCK_VOLT_STEP1;
117:     }
118:   else
119:     {
120:       return RK806_BUCK_VOLT_MAX1;
121:     }
122: }
123: 
124: /****************************************************************************
125:  * Name: rk806_decode_ldo_voltage
126:  *
127:  * Description:
128:  *   Return the microvolt value for an LDO (NLDO/PLDO) output selector.
129:  *
130:  ****************************************************************************/
131: 
132: static uint32_t rk806_decode_ldo_voltage(unsigned int selector)
133: {
134:   if (selector < RK806_LDO_SEL_END0)
135:     {
136:       return RK806_LDO_VOLT_MIN0 + selector * RK806_LDO_VOLT_STEP0;
137:     }
138:   else
139:     {
140:       return RK806_LDO_VOLT_MAX0;
141:     }
142: }
143: 
144: /****************************************************************************
145:  * Name: rk806_get_voltage_count
146:  *
147:  * Description:
148:  *   Return the number of selectors for the given output family.
149:  *
150:  ****************************************************************************/
151: 
152: static unsigned int rk806_get_voltage_count(unsigned int id)
153: {
154:   if (id >= RK806_ID_NLDO1)
155:     {
156:       return RK806_LDO_SEL_COUNT;
157:     }
158:   else
159:     {
160:       return RK806_BUCK_SEL_COUNT;
161:     }
162: }
163: 
164: /****************************************************************************
165:  * Chip-side output table.
166:  *
167:  * One entry per RK806 output, in RK806_ID_* order.  These values are fixed by
168:  * the PMIC; the board supplies everything else in its rk806_rail_cfg table.
169:  */
170: 
171: #define RK806_BUCK_HW(_id, _ereg, _emask)                               \
172:   {                                                                     \
173:     RK806_REG_BUCK##_id##_ON_VSEL, RK806_BUCK_VSEL_MASK, _ereg, _emask, \
174:         RK806_BUCK_SEL_COUNT                                            \
175:   }
176: 
177: #define RK806_NLDO_HW(_id, _ereg, _emask)                               \
178:   {                                                                     \
179:     RK806_REG_NLDO##_id##_ON_VSEL, RK806_NLDO_VSEL_MASK, _ereg, _emask, \
180:         RK806_LDO_SEL_COUNT                                             \
181:   }
182: 
183: #define RK806_PLDO_HW(_id, _ereg, _emask)                               \
184:   {                                                                     \
185:     RK806_REG_PLDO##_id##_ON_VSEL, RK806_PLDO_VSEL_MASK, _ereg, _emask, \
186:         RK806_LDO_SEL_COUNT                                             \
187:   }
188: 
189: static const struct rk806_hw_s g_rk806_hw[RK806_NUM_OUTPUTS] = {
190:   [RK806_ID_BUCK1] = RK806_BUCK_HW(1, RK806_BUCK1_EN_REG, RK806_BUCK1_EN_MASK),
191:   [RK806_ID_BUCK2] = RK806_BUCK_HW(2, RK806_BUCK2_EN_REG, RK806_BUCK2_EN_MASK),
192:   [RK806_ID_BUCK3] = RK806_BUCK_HW(3, RK806_BUCK3_EN_REG, RK806_BUCK3_EN_MASK),
193:   [RK806_ID_BUCK4] = RK806_BUCK_HW(4, RK806_BUCK4_EN_REG, RK806_BUCK4_EN_MASK),
194:   [RK806_ID_BUCK5] = RK806_BUCK_HW(5, RK806_BUCK5_EN_REG, RK806_BUCK5_EN_MASK),
195:   [RK806_ID_BUCK6] = RK806_BUCK_HW(6, RK806_BUCK6_EN_REG, RK806_BUCK6_EN_MASK),
196:   [RK806_ID_BUCK7] = RK806_BUCK_HW(7, RK806_BUCK7_EN_REG, RK806_BUCK7_EN_MASK),
197:   [RK806_ID_BUCK8] = RK806_BUCK_HW(8, RK806_BUCK8_EN_REG, RK806_BUCK8_EN_MASK),
198:   [RK806_ID_BUCK9] = RK806_BUCK_HW(9, RK806_BUCK9_EN_REG, RK806_BUCK9_EN_MASK),
199:   [RK806_ID_BUCK10] =
200:       RK806_BUCK_HW(10, RK806_BUCK10_EN_REG, RK806_BUCK10_EN_MASK),
201: 
202:   [RK806_ID_NLDO1] = RK806_NLDO_HW(1, RK806_NLDO1_EN_REG, RK806_NLDO1_EN_MASK),
203:   [RK806_ID_NLDO2] = RK806_NLDO_HW(2, RK806_NLDO2_EN_REG, RK806_NLDO2_EN_MASK),
204:   [RK806_ID_NLDO3] = RK806_NLDO_HW(3, RK806_NLDO3_EN_REG, RK806_NLDO3_EN_MASK),
205:   [RK806_ID_NLDO4] = RK806_NLDO_HW(4, RK806_NLDO4_EN_REG, RK806_NLDO4_EN_MASK),
206:   [RK806_ID_NLDO5] = RK806_NLDO_HW(5, RK806_NLDO5_EN_REG, RK806_NLDO5_EN_MASK),
207: 
208:   [RK806_ID_PLDO1] = RK806_PLDO_HW(1, RK806_PLDO1_EN_REG, RK806_PLDO1_EN_MASK),
209:   [RK806_ID_PLDO2] = RK806_PLDO_HW(2, RK806_PLDO2_EN_REG, RK806_PLDO2_EN_MASK),
210:   [RK806_ID_PLDO3] = RK806_PLDO_HW(3, RK806_PLDO3_EN_REG, RK806_PLDO3_EN_MASK),
211:   [RK806_ID_PLDO4] = RK806_PLDO_HW(4, RK806_PLDO4_EN_REG, RK806_PLDO4_EN_MASK),
212:   [RK806_ID_PLDO5] = RK806_PLDO_HW(5, RK806_PLDO5_EN_REG, RK806_PLDO5_EN_MASK),
213:   [RK806_ID_PLDO6] = RK806_PLDO_HW(6, RK806_PLDO6_EN_REG, RK806_PLDO6_EN_MASK),
214: };
215: 
216: #undef RK806_PLDO_HW
217: #undef RK806_NLDO_HW
218: #undef RK806_BUCK_HW
219: 
220: _Static_assert(sizeof(g_rk806_hw) / sizeof(g_rk806_hw[0]) == RK806_NUM_OUTPUTS,
221:                "RK806 hardware table does not match the output ID enum");
222: 
223: /* Descriptors are filled from the board table at registration time. */
224: 
225: static struct regulator_desc_s g_rk806_regulators[RK806_NUM_OUTPUTS];
226: 
227: /****************************************************************************
228:  * Private Functions
229:  ****************************************************************************/
230: 
231: /****************************************************************************
232:  * Name: rk806_read_reg
233:  *
234:  * Description:
235:  *   Read a single 8-bit register from the RK806 over I2C.
236:  *
237:  ****************************************************************************/
238: 
239: static int rk806_read_reg(FAR struct rk806_dev_s *priv, uint8_t reg,
240:                           FAR uint8_t *value)
241: {
242:   struct i2c_msg_s msg[2];
243:   uint8_t regbuf[1];
244:   int ret;
245: 
246:   regbuf[0] = reg;
247: 
248:   /* First message: write the 8-bit register address (no stop). */
249: 
250:   msg[0].frequency = priv->frequency;
251:   msg[0].addr = priv->addr;
252:   msg[0].flags = 0;
253:   msg[0].buffer = regbuf;
254:   msg[0].length = 1;
255: 
256:   /* Second message: read back one byte. */
257: 
258:   msg[1].frequency = priv->frequency;
259:   msg[1].addr = priv->addr;
260:   msg[1].flags = I2C_M_READ;
261:   msg[1].buffer = value;
262:   msg[1].length = 1;
263: 
264:   ret = I2C_TRANSFER(priv->i2c, msg, 2);
265:   if (ret < 0)
266:     {
267:       _err("ERROR: rk806_read_reg(0x%02x) failed: %d\n", reg, ret);
268:       return ret;
269:     }
270: 
271:   return OK;
272: }
273: 
274: /****************************************************************************
275:  * Name: rk806_write_reg
276:  *
277:  * Description:
278:  *   Write a single 8-bit register to the RK806 over I2C.
279:  *
280:  ****************************************************************************/
281: static int rk806_write_reg(FAR struct rk806_dev_s *priv, uint8_t reg,
282:                            uint8_t value)
283: {
284:   struct i2c_msg_s msg;
285:   uint8_t buffer[2];
286:   int ret;
287: 
288:   buffer[0] = reg;
289:   buffer[1] = value;
290: 
291:   msg.frequency = priv->frequency;
292:   msg.addr = priv->addr;
293:   msg.flags = 0;
294:   msg.buffer = buffer;
295:   msg.length = 2;
296: 
297:   ret = I2C_TRANSFER(priv->i2c, &msg, 1);
298:   if (ret < 0)
299:     {
300:       _err("ERROR: rk806_write_reg(0x%02x) failed: %d\n", reg, ret);
301:       return ret;
302:     }
303: 
304:   return OK;
305: }
306: 
307: /****************************************************************************
308:  * Name: rk806_list_voltage
309:  *
310:  * Description:
311:  *   Return the microvolt value for a given vsel selector of the output
312:  *   identified by rdev->desc->id.
313:  *
314:  ****************************************************************************/
315: 
316: static int rk806_list_voltage(FAR struct regulator_dev_s *rdev,
317:                               unsigned int selector)
318: {
319:   unsigned int id = rdev->desc->id;
320: 
321:   if (id >= RK806_NUM_OUTPUTS || selector >= rk806_get_voltage_count(id))
322:     {
323:       return -EINVAL;
324:     }
325: 
326:   if (id >= RK806_ID_NLDO1)
327:     {
328:       return (int)rk806_decode_ldo_voltage(selector);
329:     }
330:   else
331:     {
332:       return (int)rk806_decode_buck_voltage(selector);
333:     }
334: }
335: 
336: /****************************************************************************
337:  * Name: rk806_set_voltage_sel
338:  *
339:  * Description:
340:  *   Program the ON_VSEL register of the given output with `selector`.
341:  *
342:  ****************************************************************************/
343: 
344: static int rk806_set_voltage_sel(FAR struct regulator_dev_s *rdev,
345:                                  unsigned int selector)
346: {
347:   FAR struct rk806_dev_s *priv = rdev->priv;
348:   FAR const struct regulator_desc_s *reg = rdev->desc;
349: 
350:   if (selector >= rk806_get_voltage_count(reg->id))
351:     {
352:       return -EINVAL;
353:     }
354: 
355:   return rk806_write_reg(priv, reg->vsel_reg, selector & reg->vsel_mask);
356: }
357: 
358: /****************************************************************************
359:  * Name: rk806_get_voltage_sel
360:  *
361:  * Description:
362:  *   Read the current vsel selector from the ON_VSEL register.
363:  *
364:  ****************************************************************************/
365: 
366: static int rk806_get_voltage_sel(FAR struct regulator_dev_s *rdev)
367: {
368:   FAR struct rk806_dev_s *priv = rdev->priv;
369:   FAR const struct regulator_desc_s *reg = rdev->desc;
370:   uint8_t val;
371:   int ret;
372: 
373:   ret = rk806_read_reg(priv, reg->vsel_reg, &val);
374:   if (ret < 0)
375:     {
376:       return ret;
377:     }
378: 
379:   return val & reg->vsel_mask;
380: }
381: 
382: /****************************************************************************
383:  * Name: rk806_enable
384:  *
385:  * Description:
386:  *   Enable (power up) the given output.
387:  *
388:  *   The POWER_EN register uses a write-mask protocol: the low 4 bits are
389:  *   the output state and the high 4 bits are the corresponding update mask
390:  *   (bit0<->bit4, bit1<->bit5, bit2<->bit6, bit3<->bit7).  Only bits whose
391:  *   mask is set are updated by the write, so this is NOT a read-modify-write
392:  *   operation.
393:  *
394:  *   reg->enable_mask holds the low-4-bit state bit of the output.  To drive
395:  *   it on we must write both the state bit (1) and its matching mask bit
396:  *   (state bit << 4).
397:  *
398:  ****************************************************************************/
399: 
400: static int rk806_enable(FAR struct regulator_dev_s *rdev)
401: {
402:   FAR struct rk806_dev_s *priv = rdev->priv;
403:   FAR const struct regulator_desc_s *reg = rdev->desc;
404:   uint8_t value;
405: 
406:   /* state bit set (enable) + corresponding mask bit = (state << 4) */
407: 
408:   value = (uint8_t)(reg->enable_mask | (reg->enable_mask << 4));
409:   return rk806_write_reg(priv, reg->enable_reg, value);
410: }
411: 
412: /****************************************************************************
413:  * Name: rk806_is_enabled
414:  *
415:  * Description:
416:  *   Return 1 if the output is enabled, 0 if disabled.
417:  *
418:  *   Only the low 4 bits of POWER_EN hold output state (the high 4 bits are
419:  *   the write mask), so we test the state bit against the low nibble.
420:  *
421:  ****************************************************************************/
422: 
423: static int rk806_is_enabled(FAR struct regulator_dev_s *rdev)
424: {
425:   FAR struct rk806_dev_s *priv = rdev->priv;
426:   FAR const struct regulator_desc_s *reg = rdev->desc;
427:   uint8_t val;
